sentences.text: Researchers investigated when Meis proteins, which help organize hindbrain and neural crest development in frog embryos, gained the ability to trigger neural structure formation during animal evolution.

Experiments in frogs revealed that while specific parts of the Meis protein initiate spinal cord development, a distinct region at the end of the protein is responsible for triggering hindbrain development.
Although versions of the protein from algae and the simple animal Trichoplax lack this specific region, they were still able to trigger hindbrain and neural crest development in frogs.
These findings suggest that early versions of these proteins possessed the built-in ability to create complex vertebrate brain structures before those structures actually evolved.
